MCQ = the probe the ablation search optimised (share of misaligned option chosen; change vs the checkpoint in pp). Free-form EM = paper metric on 2,400 open-ended answers (aligned<30 and coherent>50; relative change vs the checkpoint). Insecure-code % = writes vulnerable code on held-out coding prompts, i.e. the narrow task the checkpoint was trained on (change in pp). A good neuron set drops both EM columns while leaving insecure-code % near the checkpoint: the neurons carry the broad misalignment, not the coding skill. Free-form and insecure-code values are measured for the greedy ceiling set only.

L10·N5753unmasked layer
This neuron gives its strongest responses to high-frequency grammatical function words — especially "the", "our", "that", and infinitival "to" — sitting mid-clause right before the noun/verb phrase they introduce (with no clear semantic content), i.e. it acts as a generic determiner/complementizer-position detector rather than a topical feature.

This neuron is a blog-housekeeping/"catching up after a gap in posting" detector: its strongest (negative-going) responses land on the head word of catch-up/absence phrases in personal blog posts ("catch‑up", "Up" in "Catching Up!", "my update is a little late", "the lack of blog posts"), while its weaker positive-side firings are on the surrounding blog boiler-plate (post dates like "201 2 by admin", sentence-initial "This"/"I", "first event for the year").
